paragraph_context: Probabilities come from the squared magnitude \(|c|^2 = c^*c\). Direct squaring of a complex amplitude can return a negative or complex number, which no probability can equal.
readability_reason: It clearly contrasts ordinary complex squaring with squared magnitude and gives an immediately understandable reason probabilities cannot be the former.
rigor_reason: For a complex amplitude c, c^2 can indeed be nonreal or negative, whereas probabilities are real and nonnegative.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: The column \((\alpha,\beta)^T\) belongs to a stated basis.
paragraph_context: The column \((\alpha,\beta)^T\) belongs to a stated basis. Changing the reference measurement changes the entries, so the numbers have meaning only alongside the basis that produced them.
readability_reason: The relation between the displayed coordinate column and a basis is stated directly; “stated basis” presumes prior introduction of coordinates in a vector space.
rigor_reason: Coordinates such as (α,β)^T are defined relative to a chosen ordered basis.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: Changing the reference measurement changes the entries, so the numbers have meaning only alongside the basis that produced them.
paragraph_context: The column \((\alpha,\beta)^T\) belongs to a stated basis. Changing the reference measurement changes the entries, so the numbers have meaning only alongside the basis that produced them.
readability_reason: The intended point is accessible, but “changing the reference measurement” is less precise than changing the coordinate basis, and the phrase “basis that produced them” is awkward.
rigor_reason: Coordinate entries change under a basis change, but changing a measurement is not automatically identical to changing the state-vector coordinate basis without an explicit identification of measurement eigenbases.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: Overall phase leaves every prediction unchanged; relative phase shifts interference fringes.
paragraph_context: Overall phase leaves every prediction unchanged; relative phase shifts interference fringes. Confusing the shared factor with the internal phase difference misidentifies which quantities an experiment can resolve.
readability_reason: The two claims are concise but introduce “overall phase,” “relative phase,” and “interference fringes” without explanation in the sentence itself.
rigor_reason: Global phase does not affect quantum predictions, and relative phase can alter interference; the latter requires an interference-sensitive measurement arrangement.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: Confusing the shared factor with the internal phase difference misidentifies which quantities an experiment can resolve.
paragraph_context: Overall phase leaves every prediction unchanged; relative phase shifts interference fringes. Confusing the shared factor with the internal phase difference misidentifies which quantities an experiment can resolve.
readability_reason: The warning is understandable from the previous sentence, but “shared factor” and “internal phase difference” are not independently defined here.
rigor_reason: Confusing global phase with relative phase does lead to incorrect claims about observable quantities, although the exact resolvable quantities depend on the measurement setup.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: An expectation value averages many identically prepared runs.
paragraph_context: An expectation value averages many identically prepared runs. That average can fall between the allowed readings, so it can take values that no single run reports.
readability_reason: It gives a straightforward operational description of an expectation value using repeated preparation and averaging.
rigor_reason: An expectation value is an ensemble mean and is estimated by averages over identically prepared runs; strictly, it is not itself necessarily defined as a finite-run average.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: That average can fall between the allowed readings, so it can take values that no single run reports.
paragraph_context: An expectation value averages many identically prepared runs. That average can fall between the allowed readings, so it can take values that no single run reports.
readability_reason: The distinction between an average and an individual allowed reading is stated clearly and follows naturally from the preceding sentence.
rigor_reason: An expectation value can lie between discrete measurement eigenvalues and therefore need not equal any result of a single run.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: Postselection includes a projection that discards the blocked outcomes.
paragraph_context: Postselection includes a projection that discards the blocked outcomes. Unitary evolution of the atom alone cannot produce that discarding; the larger atom–magnet evolution stays unitary before the detector condition is applied.
readability_reason: “Postselection,” “projection,” and “blocked outcomes” require prior conceptual setup, though the basic idea is conveyed.
rigor_reason: Postselection conditions on selected outcomes and can be represented by projection in an ideal projective model, but postselection is more general than literal projection and discarding is an operational conditioning step.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: Unitary evolution of the atom alone cannot produce that discarding; the larger atom–magnet evolution stays unitary before the detector condition is applied.
paragraph_context: Postselection includes a projection that discards the blocked outcomes. Unitary evolution of the atom alone cannot produce that discarding; the larger atom–magnet evolution stays unitary before the detector condition is applied.
readability_reason: The contrast between unitary evolution and discarding is useful, but “detector condition” and the atom–magnet enlarged-system distinction are compressed.
rigor_reason: Unitary evolution of the atom alone cannot implement a selective discard map; modeling apparatus jointly can preserve unitary evolution before conditioning, subject to including relevant environmental degrees of freedom when needed.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: Hermitian operators label measurable quantities in this framework; unitary operators preserve inner products during evolution.
paragraph_context: Hermitian operators label measurable quantities in this framework; unitary operators preserve inner products during evolution. A Pauli matrix happens to satisfy both definitions, while most operators satisfy neither.
readability_reason: The sentence provides short functional characterizations of Hermitian and unitary operators, with terminology appropriate for mathematics PhD readers.
rigor_reason: Hermitian operators represent observables in the standard finite-dimensional framework and unitary operators preserve inner products; “label measurable quantities” is a mild simplification of the observable formalism.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: Specification of a pure-state experiment: A normalized ket, taken up to an overall phase, carries the predictions.
paragraph_context: Specification of a pure-state experiment: A normalized ket, taken up to an overall phase, carries the predictions. Each measurement reports one of its eigenvalues with the Born probability, and the Hamiltonian advances the ket between measurements.
readability_reason: The colon heading and terms “normalized ket” and “overall phase” make this denser than surrounding prose, though mathematics PhD readers can parse it with prior definitions.
rigor_reason: A normalized ray represents a pure state and is invariant under overall phase; with the measurement and dynamical data in the paragraph, it determines the predictions. The ket alone does not determine all experimental predictions absent those additional specifications.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: Each measurement reports one of its eigenvalues with the Born probability, and the Hamiltonian advances the ket between measurements.
paragraph_context: Specification of a pure-state experiment: A normalized ket, taken up to an overall phase, carries the predictions. Each measurement reports one of its eigenvalues with the Born probability, and the Hamiltonian advances the ket between measurements.
readability_reason: It compresses several specialist notions—eigenvalues, Born probability, Hamiltonian, and temporal evolution—into one sentence without a bridge from the nonphysics vocabulary assumption.
rigor_reason: The statement is materially overbroad: the eigenvalue/Born-rule wording applies directly to ideal projective measurements, and Hamiltonian evolution of a ket requires a closed-system and time-evolution qualification; generalized measurements need not report an observable eigenvalue.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: Conversion of an amplitude into a probability: The amplitude for outcome \(j\) is \(\langle a_j|\psi\rangle\).
paragraph_context: Conversion of an amplitude into a probability: The amplitude for outcome \(j\) is \(\langle a_j|\psi\rangle\). Its squared magnitude gives the probability: \(P(j) = |\langle a_j|\psi\rangle|^2\).
readability_reason: The displayed formula is standard and concise, but the heading-like lead-in and bra–ket notation require prior explanation.
rigor_reason: ⟨a_j|ψ⟩ is the amplitude for outcome j when |a_j⟩ is the corresponding normalized measurement-basis vector in an ideal projective measurement; those conditions are not stated in this sentence.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: Its squared magnitude gives the probability: \(P(j) = |\langle a_j|\psi\rangle|^2\).
paragraph_context: Conversion of an amplitude into a probability: The amplitude for outcome \(j\) is \(\langle a_j|\psi\rangle\). Its squared magnitude gives the probability: \(P(j) = |\langle a_j|\psi\rangle|^2\).
readability_reason: It directly connects the previously defined amplitude to its squared-modulus probability and states the formula clearly.
rigor_reason: This is the Born rule for a normalized state and an orthonormal measurement basis; those assumptions are supplied by the surrounding discussion but not repeated here.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: Normalization in the \(z\) basis: The condition \(|\alpha|^2 + |\beta|^2 = 1\) holds because the atom must land in one of the two \(z\)-basis outcomes.
paragraph_context: Normalization in the \(z\) basis: The condition \(|\alpha|^2 + |\beta|^2 = 1\) holds because the atom must land in one of the two \(z\)-basis outcomes.
readability_reason: The normalization equation and its two-outcome intuition are clear, though the roles of alpha and beta are assumed from earlier context.
rigor_reason: For a normalized two-component state in the z basis, the equation follows from completeness of the two outcomes; the sentence leaves that basis-expansion assumption implicit.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: Failure of a non-Hermitian measurement operator: A non-Hermitian \(A\) can have complex eigenvalues that no meter could report, and its eigenstates for different readings can overlap, so distinct outcomes would fail to exclude each other.
paragraph_context: Failure of a non-Hermitian measurement operator: A non-Hermitian \(A\) can have complex eigenvalues that no meter could report, and its eigenstates for different readings can overlap, so distinct outcomes would fail to exclude each other.
readability_reason: The central point is intelligible, but phrases such as "meter could report" and "exclude each other" are informal and compress several ideas.
rigor_reason: A non-Hermitian operator can indeed have nonreal eigenvalues and nonorthogonal eigenvectors, making it unsuitable as a standard projective observable; the wording appropriately says "can" but does not distinguish all possible non-Hermitian cases.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: Difference between unitary evolution and postselection: Unitary evolution keeps every inner product fixed.
paragraph_context: Difference between unitary evolution and postselection: Unitary evolution keeps every inner product fixed. Keeping one measurement output projects onto the corresponding subspace and renormalizes the survivor.
readability_reason: It is a short, clear statement once unitary evolution and inner products have been introduced.
rigor_reason: Unitary operators preserve every Hilbert-space inner product exactly.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment

readability_reason: The intended contrast is understandable, but "keeping one measurement output" and "survivor" are informal shorthand.
rigor_reason: The statement is correct for ideal projective measurement followed by conditioning on an outcome, but general measurements need not be projections onto a subspace in this simple form.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment
text: Outcomes after the sequence \(z+\), then \(x+\), then \(z\): The final measurement gives \(z+\) and \(z-\) with probability one half each.
paragraph_context: Outcomes after the sequence \(z+\), then \(x+\), then \(z\): The final measurement gives \(z+\) and \(z-\) with probability one half each. A magnet that only read out a prior \(x\) value while keeping \(z+\) intact would send every survivor back to \(z+\), contrary to what the three-magnet sequence records.
readability_reason: The sequence and the equal final probabilities are stated plainly, with notation established by the preceding material.
rigor_reason: Starting with z+ and postselecting x+ gives an x+ state, whose subsequent z measurement has probabilities one half and one half; the postselection assumption is implicit in the abbreviated sequence notation.

unit_title: Chapter 1 — Discrete outcomes in the Stern–Gerlach experiment

rigor_reason: Under the stated nondisturbing-readout hypothesis, survivors would remain z+, so the contrast is sound; however, the hypothetical measurement model is informal and not mathematically specified.

text: For basis operators, the partial trace satisfies \[ \operatorname{Tr}_B\left(|a b\rangle\langle a' b'|\right) =\langle b'|b\rangle\,|a\rangle\langle a'| =\delta_{b'b}|a\rangle\langle a'|, \] where the Kronecker delta \(\delta_{b'b}\) equals 1 when \(b'=b\) and 0 otherwise.

readability_reason: The formula is mathematically explicit and the delta is defined, but the nested notation makes it dense.
rigor_reason: This is the correct partial-trace identity for product basis operators, with the stated orthonormal-basis Kronecker delta.

text: Solution: Matching the four amplitudes would require \(ac=1/\sqrt2\), \(ad=0\), \(bc=0\), and \(bd=1/\sqrt2\).
paragraph_context: Solution: Matching the four amplitudes would require \(ac=1/\sqrt2\), \(ad=0\), \(bc=0\), and \(bd=1/\sqrt2\). The first condition implies \(a,c\neq0\), so \(d=0\), after which \(bd\) cannot equal \(1/\sqrt2\).
readability_reason: The contradiction argument is compact and valid, but the candidate product-state parametrization supplying \(a,b,c,d\) is implicit, so a reader must reconstruct the bridge.
rigor_reason: For a product vector \((a|0\rangle+b|1\rangle)\otimes(c|0\rangle+d|1\rangle)\), matching the Bell-state amplitudes gives the displayed equations, and they yield the stated contradiction.

unit_title: Chapter 7 — Nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond
text: Color centers form through several fabrication routes.
paragraph_context: Color centers form through several fabrication routes. Impurity atoms enter the lattice during chemical-vapor-deposition, or CVD, growth. Focused ion implantation followed by annealing places impurities and then heals the lattice. Vacancy creation near pre-existing dopants allows complexes to assemble. Femtosecond-laser processing writes vacancies locally. Annealing is controlled heating that promotes vacancy motion and defect formation. Nanopillars, waveguides, and photonic-crystal cavities subsequently improve photon collection or coupling to an optical cavity. Each fabrication step can introduce strain, surface charge noise, paramagnetic damage, or spectral diffusion, which is a time-dependent fluctuation of the optical transition frequency [R082].
readability_reason: The general claim is short and understandable, with only color centers being technical.
rigor_reason: A broad but reasonable statement that does not imply the listed routes are exhaustive.

For the axial field \(B_z = 10\) mT, its frequency contribution is \[ (28.0\ \mathrm{GHz/T})(0.010\ \mathrm T) = 0.280\ \mathrm{GHz}. \] Therefore, the two microwave transition frequencies from \(|0\rangle\) are given by \(D \pm \gamma_e B_z\), where \(D\) is the zero-field splitting and \(\gamma_e\) is the electron gyromagnetic ratio. text: Interpretation of a 10 ms CPMG result.

paragraph_context: For the specific objective of a dense and controllable architecture of interacting defects, the evidence available as of 24 August 2026 does not make sapphire competitive with diamond in demonstrated end-to-end qubit capability. The missing demonstrations required for that capability are spin-selective optical readout from a single center, modern measurements of single-center \(T_2\) and gate fidelities, deterministic and verified defect placement, coherent gates between selected sapphire defects, and scalable nanophotonic integration around those defects. Aluminum nuclei are present in every lattice cell, so the unavoidable \({}^{27}\text{Al}\) nuclear-spin bath provides a source of magnetic noise and dephasing, and this magnetic noise is an additional materials disadvantage.

rigor_reason: The conclusion is appropriately limited to demonstrated capability and a specified date, but it is an evidence-dependent synthesis whose completeness and comparative basis cannot be verified from the sentence alone.
flags: end-to-end qubit capability is not operationally defined

unit_title: Chapter 8 — Chromium and other defects in corundum
text: This assessment does not prove that such an architecture is impossible.
paragraph_context: This assessment does not prove that such an architecture is impossible. [Proposal] A credible program for establishing sapphire as a defect-qubit platform would first demonstrate one identified \(\text{Cr}^{3+}\) or \(F^+\) center. It would then measure the spread of precession frequencies across centers, called the inhomogeneous dephasing time \(T_2^*\), the refocused coherence lifetime called the Hahn-echo coherence time \(T_2\), repeated photon scattering that preserves the spin state, called optical-cycling behavior, and stability of the defect charge state, called charge-state stability. The next requirement would be the creation and spectral resolution of a registered pair, meaning two defects with verified placement or identity, whose coherent coupling exceeds both transition linewidths.
readability_reason: It is short, direct, and provides an appropriate logical qualification to the preceding assessment.
rigor_reason: The sentence correctly distinguishes lack of demonstrated competitiveness from impossibility and makes no stronger claim than the evidence warrants.

unit_title: Chapter 9 — Silicon carbide and related defect-spin platforms
text: The axial field moves the two transitions in opposite directions.
paragraph_context: The axial field moves the two transitions in opposite directions. text: [Experiment] Individual neutral divacancies in high-purity 4H-SiC have been optically isolated and coherently controlled; ensemble Hahn-echo coherence exceeded \(1\ \mathrm{ms}\) at low temperature [R096].
paragraph_context: [Experiment] Individual neutral divacancies in high-purity 4H-SiC have been optically isolated and coherently controlled; ensemble Hahn-echo coherence exceeded \(1\ \mathrm{ms}\) at low temperature [R096]. A Hahn echo is a pulse sequence that refocuses reversible dephasing in a spin ensemble. In isotopically purified 4H-SiC at \(5\ \mathrm K\), a single divacancy reached \(T_2=5.3\pm1.3\ \mathrm s\) using up to 16,384 dynamical-decoupling pulses, with end-to-end spin-to-charge readout fidelity \(80.8\pm0.6\%\) [R097]. Dynamical decoupling uses repeated control pulses to suppress selected environmental noise, and readout fidelity is the probability of correctly inferring the prepared state. The operating conditions qualify every part of that sentence: the five-second figure used up to 16,384 decoupling pulses at 5 K on an isolated spin, rather than a bare Hahn echo at room temperature in a dense implanted array.
readability_reason: The semicolon joins two related but distinct experimental claims, and the terms ensemble and individual introduce a distinction that requires careful reading.
rigor_reason: The claims are plausible and appropriately distinguish isolated individual control from ensemble Hahn-echo coherence, but their exact validity is source-dependent and the measurement conditions are only described broadly.
flags: individual and ensemble results have different conditions

A color center is an optically active point defect whose electronic transitions can provide spin initialization or readout; a cycling transition is one that repeatedly produces photons while approximately preserving the measured state. Relative to an optical defect lattice, silicon platforms require millikelvin operation plus elaborate gate stacks and charge reservoirs, and standard phosphorus-donor nodes lack a naturally bright cycling optical transition. Where the goal is a programmable electrical spin Hamiltonian rather than a spin–photon network, silicon is the preferred material.
readability_reason: The conditional contrast between electrical Hamiltonian control and spin-photon networking is clear, although the phrase preferred material presupposes an unstated evaluation criterion.
rigor_reason: Silicon is a strong choice for electrically controlled spin arrays, but declaring it preferred requires specifying the comparison set, performance metric, and constraints; the sentence is therefore a plausible judgment rather than a generally established conclusion.

text: The two rightmost columns rest on assumed coherence times, not measured performance records for a specific platform.
paragraph_context: The two rightmost columns rest on assumed coherence times, not measured performance records for a specific platform. The noisy benchmark assumes a free-induction coherence time \(T_2^*=1\ \mathrm{\mu s}\), whereas the quiet benchmark assumes \(T_2^*=100\ \mathrm{\mu s}\). The free-induction coherence time \(T_2^*\) characterizes phase loss without refocusing pulses. For exponential phase decay, the corresponding Lorentzian full width at half maximum is \[ \Delta\nu^*=\frac{1}{\pi T_2^*}, \] which gives linewidths of 318 kHz and 3.18 kHz, respectively. A 52 kHz coupling at 10 nm clears the quiet linewidth yet sits inside the noisy linewidth. A quoted coupling of 52 kHz therefore leaves gate feasibility open until it is compared with a linewidth measured under the same conditions.
readability_reason: The sentence clearly distinguishes assumed benchmark parameters from experimentally established platform performance.
rigor_reason: It accurately scopes the benchmark columns as assumption-based rather than measured records, avoiding an unwarranted experimental interpretation.

unit_title: Chapter 10 — Interactions between two defect spins
text: Distinction between direct exchange and superexchange.
paragraph_context: Distinction between direct exchange and superexchange. Direct exchange needs spatially overlapping orbitals: fermionic antisymmetry, the sign change of a fermionic many-body wavefunction under exchange of two identical fermions, splits the Coulomb energy by spin configuration. Superexchange instead proceeds by virtual hopping through energetically forbidden charge configurations. In the simplest model its characteristic scale is \(4t^2/U\), where \(t\) is the hopping amplitude and \(U\) is the energy cost of the intermediate charge configuration. Treating the two as equivalent gets the interaction-range law, the noise assumptions, and the placement tolerances wrong.
readability_reason: The contrast is intelligible as a heading, although both named mechanisms are unexplained.
rigor_reason: This is a topic label, not an assertive claim.

unit_title: Chapter 10 — Interactions between two defect spins
text: Cavity loss belongs in any \(J_{12}^{\mathrm{cav}}\) report.
paragraph_context: Cavity loss belongs in any \(J_{12}^{\mathrm{cav}}\) report. \(J_{12}^{\mathrm{cav}}\) is a cavity-mediated coherent interaction between emitters 1 and 2. The emitter positions enter through the local cavity-mode coupling amplitudes \(g_i\), so the interaction follows no universal \(1/r^n\) distance law. The cavity loss rate \(\kappa\) also contributes induced decay \[ (g_i/\Delta_i)^2\kappa, \] where \(\Delta_i\) is the detuning of emitter \(i\) from the cavity mode. A gate needs the coherent shift to exceed the induced decay and emitter dephasing rates; a nonzero shift alone does not qualify.
readability_reason: The sentence is brief, but it presupposes the meaning of cavity loss and the reporting quantity.
rigor_reason: Cavity loss is relevant when reporting an operational coherent cavity-mediated interaction, but “any report” is a normative and overly unconditional formulation.

unit_title: Chapter 16 — Local stabilizer checks and encoded information
text: Commutation of star and plaquette checks.
paragraph_context: Commutation of star and plaquette checks. A star operator \(A_v\) is a stabilizer check formed from Pauli \(X\) operators on the edges incident on vertex \(v\), whereas a plaquette operator \(B_p\) is formed from Pauli \(Z\) operators around plaquette \(p\). Checks of the same type commute because they use the same Pauli type. A star and a plaquette share either zero edges or two edges. Because \(X\) and \(Z\) anticommute on each shared edge, each overlap contributes an \(XZ\) minus sign. The number of such signs is even, so their product is \(+1\), and the star and plaquette commute.
readability_reason: A concise, conventional exercise label whose meaning is clear from the surrounding context.
rigor_reason: This is a topic label rather than a scientific assertion.

unit_title: Chapter 16 — Local stabilizer checks and encoded information
text: Number of logical qubits on the eight-edge torus.
paragraph_context: Number of logical qubits on the eight-edge torus. The eight edges support \(n=8\) physical qubits. There are six independent stabilizer generators: three independent stars and three independent plaquettes. The remaining checks are constrained by the relations \(\prod_v A_v=I\) and \(\prod_p B_p=I\), where \(I\) is the identity operator. Thus the stabilizer rank is \(r=6\). For a stabilizer code, the number of encoded logical qubits is \(k=n-r\), so \(k=n-r=8-6=2\). The ground-state subspace therefore contains four states.
readability_reason: A clear and specific exercise label.
rigor_reason: This is a topic label rather than a scientific assertion.

paragraph_context: Abelian character of the anyons. Fusion specifies the total topological charge obtained by combining anyons. The fusion outcomes are unique, so each fusion space—the state space associated with a fixed set of anyons and fusion outcomes—is one-dimensional. Braiding therefore multiplies the state by a phase, such as \(-1\), rather than mixing a vector of fusion amplitudes. The anyons are Abelian even though the braiding phase is not \(+1\).
readability_reason: Clear contrast that resolves a likely conceptual confusion about Abelian anyons and nontrivial braiding.
rigor_reason: Precisely distinguishes Abelian fusion behavior from the possibility of a nontrivial Abelian braiding phase.

unit_title: Chapter 16 — Local stabilizer checks and encoded information
text: Insufficiency of the many-body gap for self-correction.
paragraph_context: Insufficiency of the many-body gap for self-correction. A many-body gap is the energy separation between the ground-state subspace and the lowest excited states. A self-correcting memory would additionally require an error-process energy barrier that increases with the linear system size \(L\). Once an anyon pair exists, either anyon can move without increasing the number of excitations. The energy barrier along a path that wraps around the system therefore remains of order \(J_e\) or \(J_m\), where \(J_e\) and \(J_m\) set the excitation-energy scales, and does not grow with \(L\).
readability_reason: As a heading it is clear, although the phrase “self-correction” is compressed and assumes the following definition.
rigor_reason: This is a heading rather than a standalone scientific assertion.

unit_title: Chapter 20 — Digital emulation and intrinsic anyons
text: Operational sequence for a digital braid experiment.
paragraph_context: Operational sequence for a digital braid experiment. A digital braid experiment represents anyons—quasiparticle excitations characterized by their fusion and exchange operations—within an encoded qubit Hilbert space. The experiment first prepares a target vacuum wavefunction, meaning the encoded state with no anyonic excitations. It then creates encoded anyon pairs, transports or exchanges them using compiled sequences of local quantum gates, transforms the resulting state into a fusion basis, and measures the fusion channel. The fusion basis labels states by the possible total topological charges obtained when anyons are combined, and the measured fusion channel identifies the resulting charge.
readability_reason: This concise heading clearly identifies the topic of the following procedure.
rigor_reason: This is a heading rather than a scientific assertion.

unit_title: Chapter 20 — Digital emulation and intrinsic anyons
text: Fusion probabilities after braiding the middle pair of four Fibonacci anyons.
paragraph_context: Fusion probabilities after braiding the middle pair of four Fibonacci anyons. Let \(P(\mathbf1)\) and \(P(\tau)\) denote the probabilities of measuring the trivial fusion channel \(\mathbf1\) and the nontrivial Fibonacci charge \(\tau\), respectively. After the middle pair is braided, the corresponding amplitudes have squared magnitudes \(\phi^{-2}\) and \(\phi^{-1}\). Thus, \[ P(\mathbf1)=\phi^{-2},\qquad P(\tau)=\phi^{-1}, \] and therefore \[ P(\tau)/P(\mathbf1)=\phi. \] Here \(\phi\) is the positive solution of \(\phi^2=\phi+1\). This identity also gives \[ \phi^{-2}+\phi^{-1}=1, \] so the two fusion probabilities are normalized.
readability_reason: This heading is concise and clearly states the subject of the calculation.
rigor_reason: This is a heading rather than a scientific assertion.

text: Do not represent all spatial disorder by a Gaussian standard deviation.
paragraph_context: Do not represent all spatial disorder by a Gaussian standard deviation. rigor_reason: A Gaussian standard deviation alone cannot characterize channeling, diffusion tails, correlations, or rare close pairs that affect dipolar couplings.

text: A dipolar graph carries dipolar couplings on its edges.
paragraph_context: A dipolar graph carries dipolar couplings on its edges. First-order uncertainty propagation for \(J\propto r^{-3}\) gives \[ \sigma_J/J\approx 3\sqrt{2}\,\sigma_{\rm site}/r. \] Here, \(J\) is the coupling strength, \(\sigma_J\) is its standard deviation, \(\sigma_{\rm site}\) is the standard deviation of each site position, and \(r\) is the nominal separation. Set the fractional coupling scatter on the left side to \(0.20\) and use \(r=20\ \mathrm{nm}\). Then \[ \sigma_{\rm site}\le 0.20\times20/(3\sqrt{2})=0.94\ \mathrm{nm}. \] Thus, under the assumptions of independent site-position errors and first-order propagation, the site-position standard deviation must satisfy \(\sigma_{\rm site}\lesssim0.94\) nm.
readability_reason: The sentence gives a compact definition, though the verb carries is slightly informal for a weighted graph.
rigor_reason: A dipolar-interaction graph can represent sites as vertices and dipolar couplings as edge weights. The wording would be more precise if it explicitly identified the couplings as weights or labels.

text: Let \(P_{S,\max}\) denote the maximum population transferred to a spectator transition, and let \(\Delta_S\) be that transition’s detuning from the applied drive.
paragraph_context: Let \(P_{S,\max}\) denote the maximum population transferred to a spectator transition, and let \(\Delta_S\) be that transition’s detuning from the applied drive. Under the far-detuned assumption \(|\Delta_S|\gg\Omega\), \[ P_{S,\max}\approx(\Omega/\Delta_S)^2. \] Setting the right-hand side to \(10^{-3}\) and inverting gives \[ |\Delta_S|/\Omega\gtrsim\sqrt{10^3}\approx31.6. \] This result applies to the stated ideal two-level bound.
readability_reason: The sentence introduces the two quantities directly, although spectator transition and detuning are specialized terms.
rigor_reason: The quantities are defined coherently for the subsequent calculation, but the interval over which the population maximum is taken and the sign convention for detuning remain implicit.

paragraph_context: The encoded state of an interacting cluster is a particular collective eigenstate or subspace of the cluster Hamiltonian. A product state in which the constituent spins are individually polarized may have poor overlap with that collective encoded state.

unit_title: Chapter 35 — Addressing and readout in dense defect arrays
text: Let \(P_C\) be the projector onto the encoded cluster subspace, \(g_j\) the coupling of physical spin \(j\) to the drive, and \(S_j^x\) the \(x\)-component spin operator for that site.
paragraph_context: Let \(P_C\) be the projector onto the encoded cluster subspace, \(g_j\) the coupling of physical spin \(j\) to the drive, and \(S_j^x\) the \(x\)-component spin operator for that site. The drive restricted to the encoded subspace is \[ P_C(\sum_j g_j S_j^x)P_C. \] If all \(g_j\) are equal and the logical states transform oppositely under a symmetry that changes the sign of the summed operator, the logical transition matrix element vanishes. The same symmetry that protects the encoded states from uniform noise can therefore make the logical transition inaccessible to a uniform microwave field.
readability_reason: The notation is introduced systematically, although the physical meanings of the projector and spin component assume some background.
rigor_reason: This is a notation-setting instruction rather than a substantive mathematical or empirical claim.

rigor_reason: Many topological logical operations involve braiding or globally supported code processes, but braiding is not the only mechanism; code deformation, measurements, and locality-preserving operations can also act logically. unit_title: Chapter 35 — Addressing and readout in dense defect arrays
text: Control operations charge physical costs and constraints.
paragraph_context: Control operations charge physical costs and constraints. Initialization must separately establish charge state, physical-spin state, and encoded-cluster state. A selective drive needs a nonempty bandwidth interval between the linewidth scale and the nearest spectator-transition or leakage scale. Crosstalk means error in the implemented operation, not a geometric property read off a beam image. Optical, microwave, spectral, and local selectors all perturb the device: global protocols preserve symmetry and save wiring without providing arbitrary routing, while local protocols gain routing flexibility at the cost of added disorder and calibration overhead. Reading a local physical spin still does not constitute logical topological readout.
readability_reason: The meaning is apparent, but the verb used for imposing costs is awkward and the claim is very abstract.
rigor_reason: Physical controls do consume resources and face constraints, but the sentence identifies neither the relevant resources nor the mechanisms, leaving it accurate only as a vague general principle.

unit_title: Chapter 36 — Measurement of topological information
text: One spin is measured by flashing an optical pulse and collecting the spin-dependent fluorescence.
paragraph_context: One spin is measured by flashing an optical pulse and collecting the spin-dependent fluorescence. The photon record then classifies the spin under its conventional “up” or “down” label. That procedure reads a specific microscopic degree of freedom with a physical detector.
readability_reason: The procedure is described concretely in plain language, and fluorescence is the only mildly technical term.
rigor_reason: Spin-dependent fluorescence is a standard readout method for suitable optically active systems, but it is not available for arbitrary spins and requires an appropriate optical transition, collection apparatus, and calibrated measurement basis.

unit_title: Chapter 36 — Measurement of topological information
text: Reading such information takes a ladder of operators and protocols.
paragraph_context: Reading such information takes a ladder of operators and protocols. Single-spin readout comes first, then tests of four-neighbor local constraints. Spectroscopy maps the energies a drive can reach. Open string operators ask whether excitations sit at their endpoints. Noncontractible closed loops separate the global sectors, and fusion experiments report the total charge when two excitations combine.
readability_reason: The ladder metaphor is understandable in context, but it may be confused with the technical quantum-mechanical term ladder operator.
rigor_reason: Multiple observables and protocols can characterize topological information, but a fixed sequence of progressively higher measurements is not generally required for every readout.

text: A quantum measurement pairs an operator with the probability distribution over its outcomes.

text: Follow the toric-code convention: one physical two-level system on every edge of a square lattice with periodic boundary conditions — a two-dimensional Hilbert space per edge, representable as a spin or qubit, with opposite boundaries identified so the lattice forms a torus.
paragraph_context: Follow the toric-code convention: one physical two-level system on every edge of a square lattice with periodic boundary conditions — a two-dimensional Hilbert space per edge, representable as a spin or qubit, with opposite boundaries identified so the lattice forms a torus. For each edge \(e\), write \(X_e\) and \(Z_e\) for the Pauli operators and define the plaquette operator \[ B_p=\prod_{e\in\partial p} Z_e, \] where \(\partial p\) collects the four edges bounding plaquette \(p\). Its eigenvalues are \(b_p=+1\) and \(-1\). At every vertex \(s\), the star operator is \[ A_s=\prod_{e\ni s}X_e, \] where \(e\ni s\) collects the four edges meeting at \(s\). The ideal toric-code ground space is the joint \(+1\) eigenspace of all star and plaquette operators: \(A_s=+1\) and \(B_p=+1\) for every \(s\) and \(p\) [R030]. [Theory]

unit_title: Chapter 36 — Measurement of topological information
text: Dependence of a contractible \(Z\) loop on the torus.
paragraph_context: Dependence of a contractible \(Z\) loop on the torus. A contractible loop is a closed path that can be continuously reduced to a point on the surface. In the ideal code, a contractible \(Z\) loop is the product of the enclosed plaquette operators \(B_p\), where each \(B_p\) is a stabilizer associated with a plaquette. Therefore, any two ground states satisfying every \(B_p=+1\) have the same eigenvalue for that loop, so the loop is not an independent logical observable. By contrast, a noncontractible loop, which cannot be continuously reduced to a point on the torus, cannot be expressed as that product and can distinguish the ground states.
readability_reason: As a section heading it is understandable, but it is a fragment and the phrase “dependence ... on the torus” is somewhat abstract without the following explanation.
rigor_reason: This is a navigation/section label rather than a substantive claim.

paragraph_context: Local spins report through calibrated transducers that convert the spin-dependent response into a detectable signal. Pauli products yield either to ancilla readout or to destructive snapshots of the constituent sites. Spectroscopy fixes energy differences. Open strings, laid along paths with distinct endpoints, test the charges at those endpoints. Closed loops and interferometers probe enclosed or logical charge. Fusion readout projects onto a defined total-charge channel. State tomography reconstructs selected state information, with full tomography costing exponentially in system size. No single method here measures topology directly. Every physical claim therefore attaches to a specific observable, documented with its definition, calibration, assumptions, and limitations.

rigor_reason: The statement is technically sound at a general level, provided the transducers are in fact calibrated and the measured response is spin dependent.

unit_title: Assessment I — The proposal and its limits
section_title: Assessment I — The proposal and its limits
text: The architectural feature under test is the grouping of defects into clusters.
paragraph_context: The architectural feature under test is the grouping of defects into clusters. Several interacting spins occupy many joint states; a well-designed cluster splits that spectrum so that two states sit well below the rest. At operating energies the cluster then moves only within that pair, and the pair functions as one effective two-state object. An isolated defect offers a fixed spin and fixed couplings, while the cluster's spectrum, wavefunctions, and symmetry become adjustable parameters that shape the effective object and its interactions.
readability_reason: The sentence is clear in context, though “architectural feature” and “clusters” are abstract design language before the next sentences supply the mechanism.
rigor_reason: It accurately identifies the proposed structural element, without yet claiming that clustering is sufficient to produce the target phase.

text: A color center is a point defect in a crystal whose internal states can be addressed optically or electronically.
paragraph_context: A color center is a point defect in a crystal whose internal states can be addressed optically or electronically. Such a defect can sense fields, link optical photons to spins, or serve as a physical qubit, and still be unsuitable for the proposal considered here. That proposal asks for a topologically ordered phase generated directly by a many-body Hamiltonian that acts continuously, rather than by programmed gate sequences. It requires the following sequence of physical and engineering steps: \[ \begin{aligned} \text{defects} &\to\text{clusters}\to\text{pseudospins}\to\text{target graph}\\ &\to\text{many-body terms}\to\text{gapped phase} \to\text{logical protection}. \end{aligned} \]

rigor_reason: This is a standard and broadly accurate characterization of a color center. It simplifies the range of color-center systems and the meaning of “addressed,” but neither simplification changes the claim in context.

text: Its message for this proposal is that a single neighborhood already contains the auxiliary and memory resources a repeated cell would draw on.
paragraph_context: [Experiment] A diamond NV register containing one electron spin, one nitrogen nuclear spin, and eight \(^{13}\)C nuclear spins demonstrated pairwise control across ten qubits and protected an arbitrary single-qubit state for more than 75 s at about 3.7 K under dynamical-decoupling control [R119]. Dynamical decoupling — repeated pulses that average away environmental noise — sustained that memory. The experiment used one defect neighborhood rather than a cluster of interacting electron defects, and the protection came from active pulses rather than from a static spectrum. Its message for this proposal is that a single neighborhood already contains the auxiliary and memory resources a repeated cell would draw on.
readability_reason: The intended proposal-level inference is understandable, but “auxiliary and memory resources” and “repeated cell” are abstract and leave the exact resource mapping implicit.
rigor_reason: The experiment demonstrates multiple controllable spins and long-lived memory, but the claim that it already contains all resources a repeated cell would draw on is an extrapolation rather than a direct experimental result.

unit_title: Five Structural Design Variables
section_title: Lower-complexity topological targets before Fibonacci order
text: [Theory] Kitaev’s honeycomb model proves that local two-body, bond-dependent spin interactions can yield emergent Majorana fermions and a non-Abelian Ising phase [R017].
paragraph_context: [Theory] Kitaev’s honeycomb model proves that local two-body, bond-dependent spin interactions can yield emergent Majorana fermions and a non-Abelian Ising phase [R017]. Majorana fermions are the self-adjoint fermionic excitations of that solution, and its non-Abelian phase exchanges them by noncommuting operations on a degenerate state space. Levin–Wen string-net Hamiltonians provide commuting-projector targets — sums of mutually compatible local projectors — for doubled topological orders, including doubled non-Abelian ones [R018]. A commuting-projector Hamiltonian is a sum of mutually commuting local projection operators. These results are existence proofs for Hamiltonians, not demonstrations in materials.
readability_reason: The model, locality, interaction order, and resulting phase are presented in a compact but coherent way; “proves” and “emergent” carry specialist mathematical-physics meaning that the next sentence partly explains.
rigor_reason: Kitaev’s honeycomb model does yield emergent Majorana fermions and an Ising-type non-Abelian phase, but the statement suppresses qualifications about parameter regimes, integrability, and the precise phase realization.

unit_title: Five Structural Design Variables
section_title: Lower-complexity topological targets before Fibonacci order
text: A defect-cluster platform can climb that ladder: first a projected bond-dependent model, then a generated stabilizer — an operator whose fixed eigenvalue constrains the many-body state — then a small topological patch.
paragraph_context: A defect-cluster platform can climb that ladder: first a projected bond-dependent model, then a generated stabilizer — an operator whose fixed eigenvalue constrains the many-body state — then a small topological patch. Passing an Abelian or Ising-type stage validates the Hamiltonian engineering while leaving Fibonacci order untested, because Abelian exchange operations commute and Fibonacci exchange operations do not. Doubled-Fibonacci order is therefore its own further target, not a corollary of the simpler ones.
readability_reason: The ladder metaphor and sequence are understandable, but “projected bond-dependent model,” “generated stabilizer,” and “small topological patch” are not fully connected by explicit operational steps.
rigor_reason: A staged progression is plausible, but the sentence presents a platform-specific development path without specifying how projection generates the effective model or stabilizer and without establishing that each stage is realizable.

readability_reason: The strategic point is clear, but the explanation relies on compressed anyon terminology and treats “exchange operations” as the sole contrast between Abelian/Ising and Fibonacci stages.
rigor_reason: Abelian braiding representations commute up to phases, whereas Fibonacci braiding is non-Abelian, but Ising anyons are themselves non-Abelian; grouping an “Ising-type stage” with an Abelian stage under this justification is materially imprecise.

A common sufficient adiabatic timescale is [R245] \[ t_f\gg\frac{\hbar\lVert dH/ds\rVert}{\Delta_{\min}^2} =\frac{1}{2\pi}\frac{10^8}{800^2}\ \mathrm{s} \approx25\ \mathrm{s}. \]

rigor_reason: The units and numerical evaluation are correct, and this is a familiar conservative adiabatic scaling estimate. Calling it a sufficient condition without hypotheses is imprecise: rigorous bounds require assumptions on the interpolation, spectral isolation, differentiability, and an error criterion, and may involve additional terms.

paragraph_context: Let \(P_A\) and \(P_B\) project onto the doublets of clusters \(A\) and \(B\), respectively. Let \(I_A\) and \(I_B\) denote identity operators in those doublets, and let \(\tau_A^z\) and \(\tau_B^z\) denote effective Pauli-\(z\) operators. Inside the doublets, \[ P_A S_{A,3}^z P_A=a_0 I_A+a_z\tau_A^z \] and \[ P_B S_{B,1}^z P_B=b_0 I_B+b_z\tau_B^z. \] Expanding the projected product shows that the \(\tau^z\tau^z\) coefficient is \(v a_z b_z\). unit_title: Common analytical errors

paragraph_context: A digital implementation tests control rather than passive emergence. text: Check of \(K/h=800\) Hz and \(K/(\hbar\Gamma)\approx5\).
paragraph_context: Check of \(K/h=800\) Hz and \(K/(\hbar\Gamma)\approx5\). Here, \(K\) is the effective high-order coupling energy, \(h\) is Planck’s constant, \(\hbar=h/2\pi\) is the reduced Planck constant, \(\Gamma\) is the decoherence rate, and \(\epsilon\) is the perturbative expansion parameter. With \(J/h=100\) MHz and \(\epsilon=0.02\), \[ K/h=100\,\mathrm{MHz}\times(0.02)^3=800\ \mathrm{Hz}. \] For \(T_2=1\) ms, \(\Gamma=10^3\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\) and \(\hbar\Gamma/h=\Gamma/2\pi=159\) Hz. The ratio is therefore about 5 rather than \(\gg1\): the effective coupling exceeds the decoherence scale by a small factor that later uncertainties can erase.
readability_reason: The numerical expressions are compact and comprehensible to a mathematician, but the physical meanings of the symbols require the following text.
rigor_reason: This is a heading announcing a calculation rather than a standalone scientific assertion.

text: This estimate holds in the dilute-activation regime, equivalently as a union bound once the per-opportunity probability is justified.
paragraph_context: This estimate holds in the dilute-activation regime, equivalently as a union bound once the per-opportunity probability is justified. A simple rate model instead gives an expected count \(\Lambda=N_s g\gamma_0 t_{\mathrm{store}}e^{-E_{\mathrm{act}}/(k_BT)}\), with attempt rate \(\gamma_0\), and Poisson probability \(1-e^{-\Lambda}\). rigor_reason: A union bound does not require independent opportunities or a dilute regime; it only requires valid bounds on the individual event probabilities. Diluteness may justify an approximation or an independent-event model, but it is not equivalent to using a union bound.

unit_title: Thermal-Seed Probability Criterion
text: \(E_{\mathrm{act}}\), in J, is the lowest energy barrier among locally accessible processes that create a harmful excitation.
paragraph_context: \(E_{\mathrm{act}}\), in J, is the lowest energy barrier among locally accessible processes that create a harmful excitation. It may differ from the clean spectral gap \(\Delta_{\mathrm{topo}}\), which is the energy difference between the relevant low-energy sector and the next excited state in an ideal disorder-free model. Boundaries, weak bonds, disorder, and multistep processes can reduce \(E_{\mathrm{act}}\). For \(N_c\) approximately independent opportunities to create an excitation, a dilute-equilibrium estimate gives \[ P_{\mathrm{seed}}\lesssim N_c g\exp\!\left(-\frac{E_{\mathrm{act}}}{k_{\mathrm B}T}\right), \] where \(g\) is a dimensionless factor that counts relevant species or channels, and \(P_{\mathrm{seed}}\) is the probability of at least one harmful seed. Requiring \(P_{\mathrm{seed}}\le\epsilon_T\) yields \[ \boxed{\frac{E_{\mathrm{act}}}{k_{\mathrm B}T}\ge \ln\!\left(\frac{N_c g}{\epsilon_T}\right)}. \]
readability_reason: The definition is grammatical and fairly direct, but 'locally accessible processes' and 'harmful excitation' carry undefined physical-model-specific meaning.
rigor_reason: As an operational definition of the relevant activation barrier, it is technically sensible. The actual barrier can depend on the allowed dynamics, bath coupling, and specified failure mechanism, which the sentence leaves implicit.

Define \(A=\max_s\|\partial_sH\|\), in J, as the largest norm of the Hamiltonian derivative along the path, and \(\Delta_{\min}\), in J, as the smallest many-body gap met on the actual path. A schematic leading adiabatic estimate is \[ \epsilon_{\mathrm{ad}}\sim \left(\frac{\hbar A}{t_p\Delta_{\min}^2}\right)^2, \] where \(t_p\) is the preparation time in seconds and \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{ad}}\) is the diabatic error. Rigorous adiabatic bounds also depend on endpoint smoothness, higher derivatives, matrix elements, and system-size scaling [R247]. [Theory] Solving for a specified diabatic-error allocation \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{ad}}^*\) gives the lower bound \[ t_p\ge t_{\min}= \frac{\hbar A}{\Delta_{\min}^2\sqrt{\epsilon_{\mathrm{ad}}^*}}. \]

rigor_reason: It precisely defines a parameterized Hamiltonian path H(s) and restricts the schedule coordinate to the interval from zero to one.

text: Small patches can mimic the signatures of a gap or topological degeneracy without establishing their persistence in larger systems.
paragraph_context: Small patches can mimic the signatures of a gap or topological degeneracy without establishing their persistence in larger systems. The extrapolation model must therefore be stated. For linear size \(L\), one gapped finite-size ansatz is \[ \Delta(L)=\Delta_\infty+a e^{-L/\xi}, \] where \(\Delta(L)\), \(\Delta_\infty\), and \(a\) are in J, while \(L\) and the correlation length \(\xi\) have the same length units. A phase claim requires a credibly positive \(\Delta_\infty>0\) and comparison with competing finite-size fits. A logical-memory claim under fixed physical noise may instead use \[ p_L(d)=A_0e^{-\alpha d}, \] where \(p_L(d)\) is the logical-error probability and the code distance \(d\), prefactor \(A_0\), and exponent \(\alpha\) are dimensionless. Improvement with distance requires \(\alpha>0\), equivalently \(p_L(d+\delta d)/p_L(d)<1\).
readability_reason: The warning is clear, but spectral gaps, topological degeneracy, finite-size effects, and thermodynamic persistence are specialist concepts.
rigor_reason: Finite systems can display an apparent energy gap or near-degenerate structure that changes with size, so observing such features at small size does not establish their persistence in the large-system limit.

For dipolar coupling, \[ J\propto r^{-3}, \] where \(J\) is the coupling strength and \(r\) is the separation. Therefore, for a fractional coupling tolerance \(\eta_J\), \[ \sigma_r\le\eta_J r/3 =0.05\times10/3 \approx0.17\ \mathrm{nm}. \]
readability_reason: The numerical tolerance statement is understandable, but dipolar coupling and standard deviation notation require technical background.
rigor_reason: The stated displacement tolerance follows from the later linearized relation between relative coupling variation and separation variation for a five percent tolerance at ten nanometers.

Multiple effective defect qubits can emulate anyons, which are quasiparticle excitations characterized by nontrivial exchange and fusion rules. unit_title: Fifteen Assessment Questions
text: Native Fibonacci topological order in a defect Hamiltonian.
paragraph_context: Native Fibonacci topological order in a defect Hamiltonian. A static or driven defect Hamiltonian could, within known physics, possess Fibonacci topological order, but the cited defect interactions do not derive such an order. A Hamiltonian is the operator that specifies a system’s energy and dynamics. A static realization would require the appropriate low-energy projectors, which energetically select the target local subspaces, together with a stable excitation gap. A driven realization would additionally require Floquet stability, meaning stability under periodic driving, and controlled energy absorption or heating. This possibility remains speculative.
readability_reason: A concise heading, though it uses specialized terminology.
rigor_reason: This is a topic heading rather than a claim.

unit_title: Fifteen Assessment Questions
text: Required hierarchy of energy and frequency scales.
paragraph_context: Required hierarchy of energy and frequency scales. The design requires the hierarchy \[ \frac{\Delta_C}{h}\gg u,\Omega,\sigma,\Gamma_{\rm decoh}, \qquad \frac{\Delta_{\rm topo}}{h}\gg \frac{k_BT}{h},\Gamma_{\rm decoh},\sigma_{\rm eff}, \] where all compared quantities have units of frequency. Here \(h\) is Planck’s constant, \(u\) is the intercluster coupling, \(\Omega\) is a drive scale, \(\sigma\) is disorder, and \(\Gamma_{\rm decoh}\) is a decoherence rate. The quantity \(\Delta_C/h\) is the cluster-gap frequency, where \(\Delta_C\) is the energy separating the encoded cluster manifold from other cluster states. The quantity \(\Delta_{\rm topo}/h\) is the many-body-gap frequency, where \(\Delta_{\rm topo}\) is the energy gap protecting the intended many-body phase. In the second inequality, \(k_B\) is Boltzmann’s constant, \(T\) is temperature, and \(\sigma_{\rm eff}\) is the effective disorder within the low-energy description.
readability_reason: It is a heading-like fragment whose intended topic is clear but which is not a complete sentence.
rigor_reason: This is a section heading rather than a mathematical or scientific claim.

text: The nearest technically justified alternative is a digitally controlled defect-spin network with active error correction.
paragraph_context: The nearest technically justified alternative is a digitally controlled defect-spin network with active error correction. Such an architecture would use individual defects or small clusters only when they provide a measured improvement in control or noise. It would prepare stabilizer states or small string-net states by applying gates, measure error syndromes, and implement anyon operations as quantum simulations. A stabilizer state is defined as the simultaneous eigenstate of a commuting set of operators. A syndrome is a set of measurements used to identify errors without directly measuring the encoded logical information. A string-net state is a many-body state described by configurations of labeled extended degrees of freedom that satisfy specified local branching and recoupling rules. Optical links or a cavity could connect spatially separated modules and thereby reduce the requirement for a dense, nearly perfect crystal lattice.
readability_reason: The proposed alternative is stated directly; the specialized architecture terminology is standard enough in context.
rigor_reason: This is a plausible recommendation, but 'nearest technically justified alternative' is a comparative evaluative claim without stated criteria or comparison against other architectures.

text: Addition and scalar multiplication fix the algebra but assign no lengths or angles.
paragraph_context: Addition and scalar multiplication fix the algebra but assign no lengths or angles. An inner product is a map that assigns a complex number \(\langle u|v\rangle\) to each ordered pair of vectors. text: Take a set of composable transformations, with a distinguished identity transformation that leaves the system unchanged.
paragraph_context: Take a set of composable transformations, with a distinguished identity transformation that leaves the system unchanged. unit_title: C.4 Topological Invariance of Braids
text: Draw particle positions along the horizontal axis and time along the vertical axis, so each particle traces a worldline.

unit_title: C.4 Topological Invariance of Braids
text: Either side of the first relation moves three neighboring strands past one another through a different intermediate picture; the relation records that the two pictures deform into each other.
paragraph_context: Either side of the first relation moves three neighboring strands past one another through a different intermediate picture; the relation records that the two pictures deform into each other. section_title: Commutation and braid relations for braid-group generators
text: With two strands the group \(B_2\) has one generator and no further relation, so \(B_2\cong\mathbb Z\): the corresponding integer counts signed crossings.
paragraph_context: With two strands the group \(B_2\) has one generator and no further relation, so \(B_2\cong\mathbb Z\): the corresponding integer counts signed crossings. For \(n\ge 3\), \(B_n\) is non-Abelian, meaning that some pairs of elements fail to commute. Sending each \(\sigma_i\) to the adjacent transposition \((i\ i+1)\) defines a surjective homomorphism \[ p:B_n\longrightarrow S_n, \] where \(S_n\) is the permutation group: a homomorphism preserves composition, and surjectivity means every permutation arises from some braid. The braids mapping to the identity permutation form the pure braid group \(P_n\), consisting of braids whose strands return to their individually labeled starting positions. Forgetting the winding is exactly what \(p\) does: \(\sigma_i^2\) is a nontrivial pure braid even though \(p(\sigma_i^2)\) is the identity permutation [R012]; [R013].
readability_reason: The conclusion follows directly from the one-generator presentation and explains the geometric interpretation.
rigor_reason: Correctly identifies B_2 with the infinite cyclic group and interprets its elements by signed crossing number.

text: For anyons, a morphism is one allowed fusion or splitting channel: one concrete way to pass from the incoming charge, or direct sum of charges, to the outgoing one.

unit_title: D.2 Morphisms Represented by Arrows
text: A simple charge is a charge object with no nontrivial decomposition as a direct sum.
paragraph_context: A simple charge is a charge object with no nontrivial decomposition as a direct sum. If \(a\) and \(b\) are distinct simple charges, they admit no morphisms between them — the superselection rule: \[ \operatorname{Hom}(a,b)=0\quad(a\ne b), \qquad \operatorname{Hom}(a,a)\cong\mathbb C. \]
readability_reason: Clear definition, though “charge object” and “direct sum” rely on the surrounding categorical vocabulary.
rigor_reason: Correctly gives the relevant notion of simplicity, assuming the charge category has direct sums.

text: Stacking defines the composite morphism \(g\circ f:a\to c\): apply the first box first, then the second.

unit_title: D.2 Morphisms Represented by Arrows
text: A category is exactly these four ingredients: objects, morphisms, associative composition, and identity morphisms.
paragraph_context: A category is exactly these four ingredients: objects, morphisms, associative composition, and identity morphisms. Wires and boxes draw the data; the category is the set of rules saying which drawings are legal and when two drawings name the same process.

paragraph_context: Here \(1\) is the vacuum — no excitation. The charges \(e\) and \(m\) are the two elementary excitations, and \(\varepsilon\) is what they form together. section_title: D.3 The Four Simple Charges of the Toric Code
text: The off-diagonal signs in \(S\) record what happens when one excitation winds around another: carrying \(e\) once around \(m\) contributes a minus sign, while winding a charge around itself contributes plus one.
paragraph_context: The off-diagonal signs in \(S\) record what happens when one excitation winds around another: carrying \(e\) once around \(m\) contributes a minus sign, while winding a charge around itself contributes plus one. unit_title: D.3 The Four Simple Charges of the Toric Code
section_title: The four simple charges of the toric code
text: The toric code has four simple charges — four labels with no finer decomposition: \[ \{1,e,m,\varepsilon\}, \] where \(1\) is the vacuum and \(\varepsilon=e\otimes m\) is the composite of the two elementary charges.
paragraph_context: The toric code has four simple charges — four labels with no finer decomposition: \[ \{1,e,m,\varepsilon\}, \] where \(1\) is the vacuum and \(\varepsilon=e\otimes m\) is the composite of the two elementary charges. The symbol \(\otimes\) combines charges; Chapter 16 often writes \(\times\) for the same operation on charge labels. The fusion rules are \[ e\otimes e=m\otimes m=\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon=1, \] \[ e\otimes m=\varepsilon, \qquad e\otimes\varepsilon=m, \qquad m\otimes\varepsilon=e. \]
readability_reason: Clear and well motivated, though “no finer decomposition” is an informal gloss for “simple.”
rigor_reason: Correctly identifies the four simple charge labels and the composite relation ε=e⊗m in the toric code.

unit_title: D.3 The Four Simple Charges of the Toric Code
section_title: The four simple charges of the toric code
text: Every pair of simple charges fuses to exactly one outcome, so there is never a multi-dimensional fusion space to choose a basis in.
paragraph_context: Every pair of simple charges fuses to exactly one outcome, so there is never a multi-dimensional fusion space to choose a basis in. Hence every simple charge has quantum dimension one. The quantum dimension \(d_a\) measures how fast the fusion-state spaces grow when many copies of the charge \(a\) fuse together. The total quantum dimension \(\mathcal D\) combines the individual dimensions by summing their squares and taking the square root: \[ \mathcal D=\sqrt{d_1^2+d_e^2+d_m^2+d_\varepsilon^2}=2. \]
readability_reason: The causal explanation is clear, though “never” and “multi-dimensional fusion space” assume the reader’s technical understanding of fusion multiplicities.
rigor_reason: Correctly links unique pairwise fusion outcomes in this theory to one-dimensional pairwise fusion spaces; the claim is appropriately read within the toric-code context.

paragraph_context: The identity \(I\) is their sum. The range of \(P\) is the retained low sector; the range of \(Q\) is the eliminated high sector. unit_title: F.2 The Schrieffer-Wolff Transformation
text: Decoupling \(P\) from \(Q\) order by order, without touching the exact spectrum, is the Schrieffer–Wolff transformation.
paragraph_context: Decoupling \(P\) from \(Q\) order by order, without touching the exact spectrum, is the Schrieffer–Wolff transformation. The name comes from the original Anderson-to-Kondo application; current usage covers any low-energy block coupled to high-energy states [R024]; [R025].

text: Emergent topological phase.
paragraph_context: Emergent topological phase. A many-body phase whose intrinsic energy landscape supports emergent quasiparticles with topological properties. Establishing the phase needs its own diagnostics — gap, ground-state sectors, braiding data — not only a prepared state that resembles one of its states. (Chapters 16 and 21.)
readability_reason: The heading is familiar to specialists, but “intrinsic energy landscape,” “emergent quasiparticles,” and “ground-state sectors” make the definition conceptually dense.
rigor_reason: The description points to appropriate diagnostics and correctly distinguishes a phase from a single prepared state, but “intrinsic energy landscape” is imprecise and the phase definition omits conditions such as a thermodynamic limit, stability, and a suitable gap or order structure.

paragraph_context: Majorana mode. An emergent degree of freedom represented by an operator equal to its own adjoint. text: Passive protection.
paragraph_context: Passive protection. Error suppression produced by the system’s energy spectrum, locality properties, or Hamiltonian, without repeated syndrome measurements and recovery operations. (First: Chapter 16, “Toric code”; limitations in Chapters 21 and 31.)

text: Toric code.
paragraph_context: Toric code. An exactly solvable spin model whose Hamiltonian contains mutually commuting star and plaquette terms. The toric code benchmarks topological order; it is not a Fibonacci model. (First: Chapter 16, “Toric code.”)

text: This review presents a systematic treatment of first-principles calculations, meaning electronic-structure calculations based on fundamental quantum-mechanical models, for charged point defects.
paragraph_context: This review presents a systematic treatment of first-principles calculations, meaning electronic-structure calculations based on fundamental quantum-mechanical models, for charged point defects. A point defect is a localized departure from the ideal crystal structure, and a charged point defect carries a net charge relative to the corresponding defect-free crystal. The review covers finite-size corrections, which compensate for artifacts introduced by finite computational cells; transition levels, which specify the Fermi-level conditions at which a defect changes charge state; and formation energies, which quantify the energetic cost of creating a defect under specified conditions. It provides a basis for determining both the conclusions that electronic-structure calculations can support and the limitations of such calculations when evaluating proposed qubit defects.
readability_reason: The sentence is understandable for a mathematically trained reader, but its terminology and nested qualification make it moderately dense.
rigor_reason: It accurately characterizes the cited review as systematically treating first-principles calculations applied to charged point defects and appropriately explains the term at a high level.

text: Kitaev’s toric-code paper established that logical information can be encoded nonlocally in a gapped two-dimensional many-body system.
paragraph_context: Kitaev’s toric-code paper established that logical information can be encoded nonlocally in a gapped two-dimensional many-body system. Nonlocal encoding distributes the logical state across extended degrees of freedom rather than associating it with a single local variable, while a spectral gap is a nonzero energy separation between the relevant low-energy states and excited states. The paper also showed how anyonic processes can manipulate the encoded information; anyons are quasiparticle excitations in two spatial dimensions whose exchanges can have statistics more general than those of bosons or fermions. This work remains the standard reference for distinguishing topological encoding from self-correction and active error correction.
readability_reason: The main claim is accessible, with “nonlocal encoding” and “spectral gap” clarified in the following sentence.
rigor_reason: This is an accurate characterization of the toric code’s nonlocal logical encoding in a gapped two-dimensional model.

text: Bravyi and collaborators quantify both the capabilities and the costs of perturbative gadgets.
paragraph_context: Bravyi and collaborators quantify both the capabilities and the costs of perturbative gadgets.
